hook.text: The Kuuk Thaayorre of Australia don't use left and right. They use compass directions—always.

buildup.text: As a result, they always know which way north is. Their spatial awareness outperforms most Westerners.

discovery.text: Lera Boroditsky showed that language influences how we perceive time, color, and even blame.

twist.text: The strong version—language determines thought—was discredited. But the weaker version holds up.

climax.text: Language doesn't imprison thought, but it does nudge it. Your mother tongue shapes your default view.

punchline.text: The words you grew up with shape how you see.

quiz.question: How does language affect thought?
options: It influences perception and default thinking patterns
It has no effect on thought
